items.title: The admissible edge sets of the next layer form a matroid that does not depend on the chosen maximally sparse set
items.author: Signe Lundqvist; Tovohery Randrianarisoa; Klara Stokes; Joannes Vermant
items.work: Sparsity greedoids and pebble game algorithms for posets
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is lemma Matroid_1 (source lines 728-732): the admissible-edge family I_j of the next layer does not depend on the chosen maximally sparse set, and is non-empty whenever the layer has edges. The proof cannot be done by a direct exchange argument, because membership in I_j is not an edge count but the minimum-defining surplus criterion displayed at 575-577; the argument at 738-763 must bound an arbitrary subset through theta_{alpha_{j-1}}, replace it by theta_{alpha'_{j-1}} via the article's surplus-independence lemma, and then reclose the inequality for every subset of the second maximally sparse set. That surplus-independence lemma is itself proved from the tight-set intersection lemma (blocks) and the surplus monotonicity lemma (Increase_when_tight), so the counted unit carries a genuine research-level matroid well-definedness argument rather than a routine verification.
